app.name: SafeMigrate
app.tagline: Check your work contract before you sign or pay.

home.trust: No registration needed. Your documents stay private.
home.scan_desc: Photograph your contract and hear what it says.
home.agency_desc: Check whether a recruiting agency is licensed.
home.cost_desc: Compare what you were asked to pay with the legal limit.
home.vault_desc: Keep proof of what you paid and signed.

scan.fee_question: How much did the agency ask for?
scan.prior_salary_question: What salary were you told at first?
scan.photo_tips: Good light, page flat, whole page in the frame, no shadow across the text.
scan.camera_why_body: The app needs the camera only to photograph your document. Nothing is taken from your phone and no photo is shared with anyone.
scan.camera_denied_help: Camera permission is turned off. Turn it on in Settings → Apps → SafeMigrate → Permissions, or choose an existing file instead.

result.low_confidence_body: Some of the text could not be made out, so parts of this contract were not checked. A clearer photo will give a fuller answer.

agency.how_to_spot_heading: How to recognise a fake agency
agency.search_hint: Type the name as it appears on the paper, or the RL number.
agency.empty_title: Check an agency before you pay
agency.empty_body: Type the agency's name or its licence number above. This works without internet.
agency.results_many: {{count}} agencies matched. Check the name carefully — several can look alike.
agency.baira_not_member: Not listed as a BAIRA member
agency.state_active_title: This licence is shown as active
agency.state_active_body: This agency appears in our copy of the government list with a licence that is active and in date.
agency.licence_alone_warning: A licence number by itself is not enough. What matters is that the status reads active — an agency can print an old or borrowed number on its signboard.
agency.state_expired_body: The licence date shown in our copy of the government list has already passed. An expired licence is not a licence.
agency.state_suspended_body: This agency appears in our copy of the government list with a suspended licence. A suspended agency may not legally recruit.
agency.state_cancelled_body: This agency appears in our copy of the government list with a cancelled licence. A cancelled agency may not legally recruit.
agency.state_not_found_title: This agency was not found in our copy of the list
agency.state_not_found_body: Not finding an agency here does not prove it is fake. Our copy of the list may be out of date, or the name may be spelled differently on your paper. But it does mean you should not pay anything until you have checked in person.
agency.not_found_action: Take the agency's name and licence number to your District Employment and Manpower Office (DEMO) and ask them to confirm it. This check is free.
agency.verify_in_person: Whatever this screen says, confirm it at your District Employment and Manpower Office (DEMO) before you hand over money.
agency.stub_warning: This app is currently running on placeholder agency data for testing. Do not rely on these results until the official list is loaded.
agency.fraud_heading: Signs to stop and ask about

legit.1: It shows you its licence certificate in the office, not only a number on a signboard.
legit.2: It gives you a signed receipt for every taka you pay.
legit.3: It names the employer and the exact job before asking for money.
legit.4: It gives you the contract to read, in Bangla, before you sign.
legit.5: Its fee is at or below the government limit for that country.
legit.6: It registers your departure through BMET and you receive a smart card.
legit.7: It leaves your passport in your hands.

fraud.1: Asks for cash and gives no receipt, or a receipt with no letterhead.
fraud.2: Asks you to send money to someone's personal bKash or bank account.
fraud.3: Pushes you to decide today, or says the price rises tomorrow.
fraud.4: Cannot show a licence, or shows only a photocopy.
fraud.5: Promises a visa before any employer or job is named.
fraud.6: Tells you to travel on a visit or tourist visa and work after arriving.
fraud.7: Says the contract will be signed after you reach the country.
fraud.8: Asks to keep your passport before you have travelled.

agency.checklist_note: These are things to check and ask about. This app cannot tell you whether an agency is honest — only a person can, and the DEMO office is where to ask.

cost.country_label: Which country are you going to?
cost.amount_label: How much are you being asked to pay?
cost.amount_hint: The total, including everything the agency has asked for.
cost.salary_label: What monthly salary were you promised, in taka?
cost.salary_hint: Optional. Used to show how many months of pay the extra amount is worth.
cost.empty_title: Compare what you were asked to pay
cost.empty_body: Choose your destination country and enter the amount. This works without internet.
cost.no_ceiling_title: No published limit for this country yet
cost.no_ceiling_body: We do not have the government's cost figure for this country, so we cannot tell you whether the amount is too high. Ask your District Employment and Manpower Office (DEMO) for the current limit before you pay.
cost.over_headline: You are being asked for more than the legal limit
cost.under_headline: This is at or below the government limit
cost.under_body: The amount you entered is within the published limit. Still get a signed receipt for everything you pay.
cost.months_of_salary: That extra amount is about {{months}} months of your salary
cost.no_average: No national average figure is available for this country.
cost.stub_warning: This app is currently running on placeholder cost figures for testing. Do not rely on these numbers until the official circular is loaded.
cost.countries_pending: Only {{count}} destination countries are loaded so far. The full list is added with the official cost circular.
cost.receipt_note: Ask for a signed receipt for every taka. Without receipts a complaint is much harder to pursue.

R01.title: Your passport would be held, with no written promise to return it
R01.explain: The contract says the employer will keep your passport, and it does not promise in writing to give it back when you ask. Many employers do this and describe it as safekeeping. Even so, holding a worker's passport is against the law in Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE, and without that written line you may not be able to get it back at the moment you need it.
R01.action: Ask for one sentence to be added before you sign: that your passport is returned to you whenever you ask for it. Photograph every page of your passport and keep the photos somewhere safe.

R02.title: You are being asked for more than the legal limit
R02.explain: The government sets a maximum amount a recruiting agency may charge for this country. The amount asked of you is above that limit.
R02.action: Ask the agency in writing why the amount is higher, and get a signed receipt for every taka you pay. An overcharge can be reported to your District Employment and Manpower Office.

R03.title: This agency's licence could not be confirmed as active
R03.explain: The agency named on this document does not appear with a valid, active recruiting licence in our copy of the government list. An agency without a live licence sits outside the system that is meant to protect you if something goes wrong.
R03.action: Do not pay anything until you have checked the licence yourself at your District Employment and Manpower Office or a BMET office. Ask to see the licence certificate in person.

R04.title: The salary is below the minimum for that country
R04.explain: The monthly pay written in this document is less than the lowest legal wage for this work in the destination country.
R04.action: Ask the agency to show you where this salary is agreed. Do not travel on a contract that pays below the legal minimum.

R05.title: Your recruitment cost would be taken out of your wages
R05.explain: The contract says the money spent recruiting you will be recovered from your salary. This is what turns a job into a debt, and it is the usual reason a worker cannot leave a bad workplace. Under international standards the employer pays recruitment costs, not the worker.
R05.action: Ask for this clause to be removed before you sign. Keep this document either way — it is evidence.

R06.title: The salary is lower than what you were first told
R06.explain: The pay in this document is less than the amount you said you were promised earlier. Changing the terms after you have paid and committed is a recognised warning sign.
R06.action: Do not sign until the salary matches what you were promised. Keep any earlier offer, message or advertisement that shows the first amount.

R07.title: The employer or the job is not clearly named
R07.explain: The document does not clearly say who you would work for, or exactly what work you would do. Without a named employer you cannot check who they are, and no one can be held responsible if you are mistreated.
R07.action: Ask for the employer's full name and address, and the exact job title, to be written into the contract before you sign.

R08.title: You may not be free to leave the job or the country
R08.explain: The document says you cannot end the contract yourself, or that you need permission to leave the country. Being able to walk away is what separates a job from forced labour.
R08.action: Ask for the right to resign with notice to be written in. Save the phone number of the Bangladesh embassy in that country before you travel.

R09.title: No return ticket home is promised
R09.explain: The contract does not say the employer will pay for your journey home. If you need to leave, the fare may be more than you can save, and you would be dependent on the employer's goodwill to get back.
R09.action: Ask for the return ticket to be written into the contract, including who pays for it if the job ends early.

R10.title: Very long hours, with no overtime rate agreed
R10.explain: The hours written here add up to more than 48 in a week, which is the international standard limit, and no overtime rate is written down. Extra hours with no agreed rate are commonly left unpaid.
R10.action: Ask for the overtime rate to be written into the contract as an actual figure, not a promise.

R11.title: The probation period cuts your pay or runs long
R11.explain: Your pay would be reduced during probation, or probation lasts longer than three months. This usually falls in the months when you owe the most and can least afford a smaller wage.
R11.action: Ask exactly what you would be paid during probation, and get that figure written into the contract.

R12.title: No weekly rest day
R12.explain: The document shows no rest day in the week. One day of rest in seven is the international standard.
R12.action: Ask for a weekly rest day to be written into the contract.

R13.title: Accommodation or food is not clearly provided
R13.explain: The contract does not clearly state that the employer provides both a place to live and food. These are often promised in conversation and left out of the paper, and their cost then comes out of your wage.
R13.action: Ask for accommodation and food to be written into the contract, and ask whether anything will be deducted from your pay for them.

R14.title: The document is not in Bangla or English
R14.explain: This document is written in a language you may not be able to read. In a dispute it is usually the written version that counts, not what was explained to you aloud.
R14.action: Do not sign until you have a Bangla or English copy, and have someone you trust read it through with you.

I01.title: Parts of the document could not be read
I01.explain: The photo was not clear enough to read every part of the document, so some checks could not be carried out.
I01.action: Take the photo again in better light, with the page flat and the whole page inside the frame.

I02.title: The contract says your passport is returned on request
I02.explain: The employer would hold your passport, and the contract states in writing that it is returned to you whenever you ask for it. That written line is what keeps the passport under your control.
I02.action: Check that this line really is printed in the contract and not just promised aloud. Keep a photo of every page of your passport.

I03.title: Several things could not be checked
I03.explain: A number of checks could not be carried out, because the document did not contain the information they need or that part could not be read.
I03.action: A clearer photo of the whole document — including the back and any extra pages — will let more checks run.

common.disclaimer: This app flags possible risks for you to check with a person. It is not legal advice and does not decide whether a document is fraudulent.
